When `props.sessionID` is missing, this still calls `session.infinitySet` with an empty `sessionID` and then updates local UI state to active even if the request fails. Avoid issuing the request without a valid session ID (and avoid flipping UI state optimistically in this case), or defer activation until a session is created/selected.
```suggestion

```

Infinity mode UI state is initialized to `{ active: false }` and only changes via `onInfinity`, but the component never queries the server for the session’s current Infinity status on load. If a user re-opens a session with Infinity already enabled, the command label/state will be wrong. Fetch `session.infinityStatus` during session bootstrap (similar to `session.get`) and call `setInfinity` accordingly, or derive it from synced session state if available.

`InfinityJudgeOutput` marks `prompt` (and `reason`) as optional, but the Infinity judge prompt requires `prompt` when `should_continue=true` and the calling code assumes it can continue even if `prompt` is missing (falls back to the assistant’s last reply). This can create non-actionable self-prompts and accidental loops. Tighten the schema/parse logic so `prompt` is required when `should_continue` is true (and either require `reason` too, or remove it from the prompt + downstream usage consistently).
```suggestion
const InfinityJudgeOutput = z.discriminatedUnion("should_continue", [
  z.object({
    summary: z.string().trim().min(1),
    should_continue: z.literal(true),
    prompt: z.string().trim().min(1),
    reason: z.string().trim().min(1),
  }),
  z.object({
    summary: z.string().trim().min(1),
    should_continue: z.literal(false),
    prompt: z.string().trim().min(1).optional(),
    reason: z.string().trim().min(1).optional(),
  }),
])
```

The Infinity judge logging includes full `raw` model output at info level. This can leak sensitive conversation content into logs and also produce very large log lines. Consider removing this log line, downgrading it to debug/trace, and/or logging only a bounded preview with redaction.

When the judge decides the session is complete, the loop breaks but Infinity mode state is never cleared from `infinityState`. That means `GET /session/:sessionID/infinity` will continue to report `active: true`, and subsequent activity could re-enter Infinity behavior unexpectedly. Clear the session’s Infinity state when `shouldContinue` is false (or otherwise persist an explicit "inactive" state).

This code still injects `[Infinity mode — ...]` user messages (and still propagates `reason`/`summary` into the conversation), but the PR description says those metadata messages and the `reason` field were removed. Either update the implementation to stop injecting these messages / remove `reason` end-to-end, or adjust the PR description to match the actual behavior.

This writes the right runtime key (`permission`), but the local `frontmatter` type above declares `permissions`, so this assignment should fail type checking with `Property permission does not exist`. Since the agent config schema reads the singular `permission` field, consider renaming the type field to `permission?: Record<string, "deny">` rather than changing this assignment.

`AVAILABLE_TOOLS` includes `write`, but the write tool is enforced through the `edit` permission key (`src/tool/write.ts` uses `permission: "edit"`). The deprecated `tools` normalizer also collapsed `write`/`edit`/`patch` into `permission.edit`, but this direct copy would generate `permission.write: deny`, which is not checked at runtime. Consider mapping `write` to `edit` here before adding the deny rule.

This `createEffect` will also track any reactive reads that happen inside `layout.projects.open(dir)` / `server.projects.touch(dir)` (e.g. `server.projects.list()`, `roots()`), so it can re-run on unrelated project-store changes and repeatedly call `touch()`/`open()`. Consider constraining the dependencies to just the decoded URL directory (e.g. using Solid's `on(resolved, ...)` pattern or `untrack` around the open/touch calls) so it only runs when `params.dir` actually changes.

`refreshDirs()` already returns whether the directory is openable. You can simplify and avoid redundant `canOpen()` scans by using its return value (e.g., early-return based on the awaited result) rather than calling `canOpen(target.directory)` again immediately after.

Same as above: since `refreshDirs(resolved.directory)` returns `canOpen(resolved.directory)`, consider using that boolean directly instead of re-checking with `canOpen(resolved.directory)` on the next line.
```suggestion
      const canOpenResolved = await refreshDirs(resolved.directory)
      if (!canOpenResolved) return false
```

Suggestion for the human reviewer to decide on: this `Math.min(half, min)` looks like it can make the `high` variant use the minimum thinking budget whenever `min` is lower than half of `max`, and can also produce a value below the API minimum if `min` is higher than half. If `min_thinking_budget` is the lower bound, this probably wants to clamp upward, e.g. `Math.max(half, min)`, so the `high` variant remains inside the supported range.

Suggestion only, and the human can decide whether it is worth changing: this introduces a new explicit `any`, which the style guide asks us to avoid. Since this value is exactly the model variants shape, using the exported model field type keeps the same behavior without spelling `any` here.

```suggestion
  const variants: NonNullable<Model["variants"]> = {}
```

`stopOAuthCallback` calls `McpOAuthCallback.stop()`, which (per oauth-callback.ts) rejects *all* pending auth callbacks and clears the pending map. Because this effect is used unconditionally (e.g., via `Effect.ensuring(...)` in authenticate/finishAuth and in removeAuth), completing/removing auth for one MCP server can inadvertently cancel a different MCP server’s concurrent OAuth flow (or another in-flight `authenticate()` call). Consider stopping the callback server only when there are no other pending OAuth flows (e.g., reference counting per flow, or a `McpOAuthCallback.stopIfIdle()` that checks pending count / `pendingOAuthTransports.size`) to avoid cross-flow interference.

This change introduces new lifecycle behavior (callback server is stopped automatically after `authenticate()` / `finishAuth()` and on auth removal/finalization), but there’s no regression test asserting that `McpOAuthCallback.isRunning()` becomes false after these code paths. Adding a focused test would help prevent reintroducing the server-handle leak (and would also cover edge cases like failure/interrupt paths where `Effect.ensuring(...)` should still stop the server).

There’s a TOCTOU window between checking existence, counting sessions, and deleting the project. If the project is deleted concurrently, this can return `{ deleted: true }` even when nothing was deleted, and `sessionsRemoved` can become inaccurate. Prefer a single transaction and/or relying on the delete result (`changes`/`returning`) to determine whether the row existed, and compute `sessionsRemoved` within the same transaction.

Same as the Hono route: deleting the project that backs the current instance can leave the cached instance context pointing at a deleted project row. Consider marking the instance for reload (or disposing it) when `ctx.params.projectID` matches the current instance’s project id so subsequent requests re-bootstrap cleanly.

This test creates a tmp directory without `git: true`, so `/project/current` will typically resolve to `ProjectID.global`. Deleting that project can cascade-delete sessions/projects created by other tests that also use non-git tmpdirs (the test DB is shared in-process via `OPENCODE_DB=:memory:`). Consider using `tmpdir({ git: true, ... })` here (or otherwise ensuring a unique project id) to avoid cross-test interference.

Deleting a project via `svc.remove(projectID)` can leave the per-directory `Instance` cache pointing at a now-deleted `Instance.project`. Subsequent requests on the same directory can return a stale `/project/current` and session creation can start failing due to a missing `project` FK. Consider disposing/reloading the instance when `projectID` matches the current instance’s project id (similar to the `initGit` route’s reload path).

`Project.remove` throws a plain `Error` on missing projects, which the server error middleware will treat as a 500. Since the route/OpenAPI annotations advertise a 404 (and callers will likely rely on it), please throw a `NotFoundError`/`NamedError` here (or otherwise return a typed 404) so the HTTP layer can correctly map it.

In the non-desktop (SyncStorage) branch, legacy-key migration now reads legacy keys from `current` storage (`migrateLegacy(... keys: legacy ...)` uses `input.current.getItem(key)`), but historically these legacy keys were looked up in `legacyStore` (unprefixed localStorage). This will prevent migrating renamed keys when `config.storage` is set (the common case for workspace/session-scoped persistence), leaving users with missing state after upgrade. Suggestion: pass `legacyStore` into `migrateLegacy` (or include it in `stores`) and read/remove legacy keys from that legacy storage instead of `current`.

`ensureChild` is now calling `Persist.workspace(key, ...)` where `key` is already normalized via `directoryKey()`. That prevents `Persist.workspace()` from generating a `legacyStorage` fallback for the *raw* directory string (e.g. Windows backslashes / trailing slashes), so existing persisted data stored under the pre-normalization workspace storage name won’t be discovered or migrated. Suggestion: keep cache/maps keyed by the normalized `DirectoryKey`, but pass the original `directory` string into `Persist.workspace(directory, ...)` (or pass both raw+normalized so `Persist` can compute legacyStorage correctly).

Minor: `legacyStore` is declared in the non-desktop branch but no longer used. If the intent is to migrate legacy keys from `legacyStore` (as before), wiring it into `migrateLegacy` will both fix migration and remove this dead local; otherwise it can be removed to avoid confusion.
